study_material.title: Number System - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: The Number System is the foundation of quantitative aptitude. Placement tests use it to check speed with divisibility, remainders, LCM/HCF, unit digits and factor counting. Most questions are formula-driven and can be solved in under a minute once the core rules are memorised.
learning_objectives: Classify numbers (natural, whole, integers, rational, irrational, prime, composite)
Apply divisibility rules for 2-11 and 19 instantly
Solve LCM/HCF problems including remainder variants
Find unit digits of large powers using cyclicity
Count factors of a number from its prime factorisation

concepts.heading: 1. Types of Numbers
concepts.body: Natural numbers N = {1,2,3,...}; Whole numbers W = N plus 0; Integers Z include negatives; Rational numbers are p/q with q not 0; Irrational numbers (pi, root 2) cannot be written as fractions. Primes have exactly two factors (2 is the only even prime); composites have more than two. 1 is neither prime nor composite. Any two-digit number with digits a,b can be written as 10a + b - this representation solves most digit-based puzzles.

concepts.heading: 2. Divisibility Rules
concepts.body: By 2: last digit even. By 3: digit sum divisible by 3. By 4: last two digits divisible by 4. By 5: ends in 0 or 5. By 6: divisible by both 2 and 3. By 8: last three digits divisible by 8. By 9: digit sum divisible by 9. By 11: (sum of digits at odd places) - (sum at even places) is 0 or a multiple of 11. By 19: add twice the last digit to the rest, repeat.

concepts.heading: 3. LCM and HCF
concepts.body: HCF is the largest number dividing both; LCM is the smallest number divisible by both. Key identity for two numbers: LCM x HCF = product of the numbers. Remainder variants: smallest number leaving remainder r when divided by a, b, c = LCM(a,b,c) + r. Greatest number dividing a and b leaving remainders r1, r2 = HCF(a - r1, b - r2).

concepts.heading: 4. Unit Digit Cyclicity
concepts.body: Unit digits of powers repeat in cycles of at most 4. 2: 2,4,8,6. 3: 3,9,7,1. 7: 7,9,3,1. 8: 8,4,2,6. 4 and 9 have cycles of 2. 0,1,5,6 never change. To find the unit digit of a^n, divide n by the cycle length and use the remainder as the position (remainder 0 means the last element of the cycle).

concepts.heading: 5. Counting Factors
concepts.body: If N = p^a x q^b x r^c (prime factorisation), the number of factors = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1). Example: 360 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 gives (4)(3)(2) = 24 factors. Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2; sum of squares = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6; sum of first n odd numbers = n^2.

concepts.heading: 6. Remainders
concepts.body: If a leaves remainder r on division by d, then a = dk + r. Remainders multiply and add: rem(a x b) = rem(rem(a) x rem(b)). Powerful trick: reduce the base modulo the divisor first, e.g. 17^200 mod 16 - since 17 = 1 mod 16, the remainder is 1.

formulas: LCM(a,b) x HCF(a,b) = a x b
Number of factors of p^a x q^b x r^c = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1)
Sum of squares 1 to n = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6
Sum of first n odd numbers = n^2
shortcut_methods: Digit-sum check (divisibility by 9) instantly validates long additions and multiplications
For unit digits, only track the last digit of the base
Greatest k-digit number divisible by d: divide the largest k-digit number by d, multiply the quotient by d
For remainder questions, reduce the base mod the divisor before applying powers
common_mistakes: Treating 1 as a prime number - it is not
Using LCM x HCF = product for three or more numbers - it only holds for two
Reading cyclicity position wrongly when the remainder is 0 (use the last element of the cycle)
Forgetting that divisibility by 6 needs BOTH 2 and 3
study_material.summary: Master divisibility rules, the LCM-HCF identity, factor counting and unit-digit cycles. Nearly every number system question in placement papers maps to one of these four tools.
quick_revision_notes: 2 is the only even prime; 1 is neither prime nor composite
LCM x HCF = product (two numbers only)
Unit digit cycles have length 1, 2 or 4
Smallest number with remainder r for several divisors = LCM + r

solved_examples.question: Find the unit digit of 7^45.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Unit digits of powers of 7 cycle as 7, 9, 3, 1 (length 4). 45 divided by 4 leaves remainder 1, so the unit digit is the 1st in the cycle: 7.
solved_examples.shortcut: Only the remainder of the exponent mod 4 matters.

solved_examples.question: Find the HCF of 84 and 126.
solved_examples.step_by_step: 84 = 2^2 x 3 x 7; 126 = 2 x 3^2 x 7. Common primes with lowest powers: 2 x 3 x 7 = 42.

solved_examples.question: Find the smallest number which when divided by 6, 8 and 12 leaves remainder 2 in each case.
solved_examples.step_by_step: LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24. The required number = LCM + common remainder = 24 + 2 = 26.
solved_examples.shortcut: Same-remainder problems: answer is always LCM + r.

solved_examples.question: How many factors does 360 have?
solved_examples.shortcut: Add 1 to each exponent and multiply.

solved_examples.question: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 72. If one number is 24, find the other.
solved_examples.step_by_step: For two numbers, LCM x HCF = product. So other number = (12 x 72)/24 = 36.

practice_questions.question: Find the sum of the natural numbers from 1 to 50.
What is the unit digit of 3^101?
practice_questions.explanation: Cycle of 3: 3,9,7,1. 101 mod 4 = 1, so unit digit = 3.

practice_questions.question: Which of the following is a prime number?
practice_questions.explanation: 91 = 7x13, 117 = 9x13, 187 = 11x17. 173 has no factor up to its square root, so it is prime.

practice_questions.question: Find the sum of the first 15 odd numbers.
practice_questions.explanation: Sum of first n odd numbers = n^2 = 15^2 = 225.

practice_questions.question: What is the largest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 88?
What is the remainder when 17^200 is divided by 16?
Is 918082 divisible by 11? Use the divisibility rule to decide.
practice_questions.explanation: (9+8+8) - (1+0+2) = 25 - 3 = 22, a multiple of 11, so the number is divisible by 11.

practice_questions.question: Express 0.363636... (36 recurring) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two numbers have HCF 13 and their product is 2028. How many such pairs are possible?
practice_questions.explanation: Let numbers be 13a and 13b with a,b coprime. 169ab = 2028 so ab = 12. Coprime pairs: (1,12) and (3,4) - 2 pairs.

practice_questions.question: Find the greatest number that divides 245 and 1029 leaving remainder 5 in each case.
practice_questions.explanation: The number divides 240 and 1024 exactly. HCF(240, 1024) = 16.

practice_questions.question: What is the unit digit of 2^50 + 3^50?
practice_questions.explanation: 2: cycle 2,4,8,6; 50 mod 4 = 2 so unit 4. 3: cycle 3,9,7,1; 50 mod 4 = 2 so unit 9. 4 + 9 = 13, unit digit 3.

topic_test.title: Number System - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for each correct answer, -0.25 for each wrong answer, 0 for unattempted.
No calculator - use divisibility rules, cyclicity and LCM/HCF identities.

questions.question: What is the sum of the squares of the first 10 natural numbers?
What least number must be added to 1000 so that the sum is divisible by 45?
questions.explanation: 1000 = 45 x 22 + 10. Next multiple is 45 x 23 = 1035, so add 35.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2^50 is divided by 7?
A number leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7. What is the remainder when twice the number is divided by 7?
Find the smallest 5-digit number exactly divisible by 89.
The unit digit of 8^33 is:
questions.explanation: Cycle of 8: 8,4,2,6. 33 mod 4 = 1, so unit digit = 8.

questions.question: Find the least number which when divided by 16, 18 and 20 leaves remainder 4 in each case.
How many numbers between 1 and 100 are divisible by both 3 and 4?
questions.explanation: Divisible by both means divisible by 12: 12, 24, ..., 96 - that is 8 numbers.

questions.question: The digit sum of a number is 27. Which of the following must divide the number?
questions.explanation: Digit sum 27 is divisible by 9, so the number is divisible by 9. Divisibility by 27 or 18 is not guaranteed by digit sum alone.
